name: Apollo 10
short_status: Completed May 26, 1969: full dress rehearsal for the Moon landing; LM Snoopy flew to roughly 47,400 ft above the surface, clearing the way for Apollo 11.
tagline: NASA · United States · Crewed orbiter · 1969 · The space race Success
stats: closest approach to the lunar surface (about 14.4 km)
reentry speed, the crewed record for 57 years
estimated viewers of the first color TV from space

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 18 May 1969, 12:49 p.m. EDT, Launch Pad 39B, Kennedy Space Center, on Saturn V AS-505

facts.label: Crew
facts.value: Thomas P. Stafford (commander), John W. Young (command module pilot), Eugene A. Cernan (lunar module pilot)

facts.label: Callsigns
facts.value: Command module "Charlie Brown", lunar module "Snoopy", after the Peanuts characters

facts.label: Lunar orbit insertion
facts.value: About 76 hours into the mission (21 May 1969); a second burn 4.5 hours later circularized the orbit at about 69 miles

facts.label: Low passes
facts.value: 22 May 1969: Snoopy undocked on the 12th revolution (about 98 hours GET), descent orbit of 9.7 by 70.5 miles, closest approach later calculated at about 47,000-47,400 ft above the surface

facts.label: Staging scare
facts.value: During LM staging Snoopy gyrated unexpectedly in all three axes; Stafford and Cernan recovered quickly, and the motions were traced to a switch set in the wrong position

facts.label: Snoopy's fate
facts.value: After redocking on May 23 (about 106 hours GET, 16th revolution), the ascent stage fired its engine to fuel depletion, leaving lunar orbit for an orbit around the Sun; asteroid-catalog object 2018 AV2 is a likely but unconfirmed match (RAS announcement, June 2019)

facts.label: Lunar orbits
facts.value: 31 revolutions over 61 hours 37 minutes in lunar orbit

facts.label: TV first
facts.value: First live color TV transmissions from space; by some estimates more than a billion people watched at least part of the broadcasts

facts.label: Reentry
facts.value: 26 May 1969: 24,791 mph at entry interface (400,000 ft), "the fastest reentry for any crewed space mission" per NASA history

facts.label: Splashdown
facts.value: 26 May 1969, 12:52:23 p.m. EDT, Pacific Ocean east of American Samoa (about 165 W, 5 08 S); crew recovered by USS Princeton, about 1.5 miles from target

timeline: Launch at 12:49 p.m. EDT from Pad 39B; translunar injection after 1.5 Earth orbits
First live color TV pictures from space, showing the S-IVB and Snoopy during transposition and docking
Lunar orbit insertion about 76 hours into the mission; orbit circularized at about 69 miles
Stafford and Cernan fly Snoopy down to roughly 47,400 ft above the Moon along Apollo 11's planned approach; brief staging gyrations traced to a mispositioned switch
Redocking with Charlie Brown; Snoopy's ascent stage burns to depletion and enters orbit around the Sun
Trans-Earth injection after 31 lunar orbits, followed by a 53-minute color telecast of the receding Moon
Reentry at 24,791 mph, the fastest crewed reentry of the Apollo era; splashdown east of American Samoa, recovered by USS Princeton
